title: Primary hyperaldosteronism: causes and the P-cell mechanism
guide: PHA = 90% acquired (B/L micronodular hyperplasia 60%; U/L adenoma 30% = Conn's) + 10% familial (Type I GRA, AD; Type II ClCN2). Aldosterone→MR→AIP (aldosterone-induced protein)→ENaC in P-cells: Na+ in, K+/H+ out; ANP activation explains no edema. Triad HTN (diastolic > systolic) + hypokalaemia + metabolic alkalosis. AME (AR, 11β-HSD2 defect) vs GRA (AD, chimeric ACTH-driven aldosterone; Rx steroids).

title: Presentation, who to screen and the drug-aware work-up
guide: HTN + proximal/distal weakness; confirm renal K+ loss (urine K+/creatinine, spot K+ ↑). ABG: acidosis → RTA; alkalosis → acquired (Cushing, PHA) vs inherited (AME AR, GRA AD, Liddle AD = ENaC gain-of-function). Normal BP + hypokalaemic alkalosis = Gitelman/Bartter. Screen every new HTN; HTN + TOD (LVH, fundus, microalbuminuria, ↑ central systolic BP) → secondary work-up. ARR obsolete; false + β-blocker/NSAIDs/clonidine, false − ACEi/ARB/spironolactone/dihydropyridine; bridge with α-blocker, hydralazine, non-DHP. Screen: PAC ≥10 ng/dl + PRA ≤1 ng/ml/hr.

title: Saline infusion confirmation and CT lateralisation
guide: Saline infusion test: 2 L NS over 4 h; normal suppression vs PHA unsuppressed (>10 ng/dL). Repeat PAC ≥10 ng/dl → CT abdomen (IOC) → B/L hyperplasia vs U/L adenoma.
